title: Times tables beyond the fact drill: the multiplication chart, properties, arrays and equal groups, and the plain × / ÷ stories (pilot unit G3-Y4.B4)

template.also: mult_chart draws on `mult-grid` (the chart to complete) and `mult-chart` (look up a product); mult_properties on `arrays-turn` (the order property: an array and the same array turned) and `equation` (identity, zero, distributive); arrays_groups on `arrays` (an array or ringed equal groups, three slots); mult_word_problems_plain / div_word_problems_plain on the story layout (`word-work`, providers/stories.js). Providers: `js/modules/sheet/providers/{multiplication,division,countby}.js`. `screen-cell.js` draws the same cells on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz.

summary: Family card for the pilot unit's multiplication skills that are not the fact drill. mult_chart: a black-and-white 12 x 12 (or 10 x 10) chart, one product looked up or a few cells filled (never the factor pairs printed in the prompt). mult_properties: the order property drawn as an array and the same array turned, identity (x 1) and zero (x 0) facts, and the distributive split. arrays_groups: an array or ringed equal groups, '__ rows of __ (groups of __). __ in all.' (three slots, one frame every item). The plain stories: one x or ÷ story per cell with no picture row, answered with a number and its unit. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing. mult_comparison (4.OA.A.1 / 4.OA.A.2, 'times as many') and remainder_interpret (4.OA.A.3, divide and say what the remainder means) are the main skills of two round-1 BUILD lessons of G4-Y5.B3 and join the story skills here.
teaches: 3.OA.A.1 (products as equal groups), 3.OA.A.2 (division as sharing / grouping), 3.OA.A.3 (x / ÷ word problems within 100), 3.OA.B.5 (properties: commutative, identity, zero, distributive), 3.OA.C.7 (know the products), 3.OA.D.9 (patterns in the multiplication table), 2.OA.C.4 (arrays to 5 x 5). WRM Y4.B4 S1 (multiples of 3), S6 (3, 6, 9 tables), S11 (x 1 and x 0), S12 (÷ 1 and itself), S13 (multiply three numbers); Y3.B4 arrays and equal groups.
research: From repo sources: design/catalogue/mult-div-integers.md (verdicts, MU-A2/A3/A7/A27/A28, MU-M1..M7), the passed detailed lessons 3a (g3-oa5-mult-properties) and 4 (g3-oa9-mult-table-patterns) and their RESEARCH.md, PROBLEM_TYPES MU rows. Reference grammar (MathWorksheets4Kids 'multiplication chart: find the missing', 'properties of multiplication', 'arrays: write the multiplication sentence'; IXL 3rd grade 'multiplication tables up to 12: find the missing factor', 'properties of multiplication', 'write multiplication sentences for arrays'): ours keeps one product or one property per boxed cell, black and white, big digits.
problemTypes: mult_chart look-up: a black-and-white chart with one row and one column shaded to a cell; write the product (the factor pair is the row and column headers, never printed in the prompt)
mult_chart fill: a chart (or a window of it) with a few cells blank; write each product
mult_properties order: an array and the same array turned; write both facts (task both), the turned fact from a known one (known), or the facts alone (missing)
mult_properties identity / zero: 'n x 1 = [ ]', '0 x n = [ ]', with counters or none
mult_properties distributive: an array split into two parts; '__ x __ = (__ x __) + (__ x __)'
arrays_groups: an array (rows of) or ringed equal groups (groups of); three slots: __ rows of __, __ in all
plain stories: one x or ÷ story (equal groups, arrays, sharing, grouping), no pictures, a number and its unit
progression: arrays / equal groups to 5 x 5 with pictures (2.OA.4, 3.OA.1) -> the order property on turned arrays -> facts alone (pictures off)
identity and zero with counters -> without (S11); divide by 1 and by itself (S12, div_by_itself)
chart look-up of one product -> fill a few cells -> find patterns (S6, lesson 4)
stories with pictures (mult_word_problems) -> plain (the _plain skills), one change a step (P-1)

drawing.sizes: digits at the working size 16 / 22 / 28 pt (S / M / L); array dots at a fixed pitch (about 9 mm) so 25 dots stay countable; chart cells at least the answer-area minimum, headers bold, the shaded row and column the single grey; answer boxes the kit's slots (SL-11).
notes: One frame per section: the slot set never changes from cell to cell (P11, SCC-T10).
No answer in the prompt: the order property never prints 'If 5 x 4 = 20, what is 4 x 5?' with both pictures; the chart prompt never lists the missing cells' factors.
Black and white only: no rainbow chart fills, no coloured array parts; the distributive split is a gap and a bracket, not colour.
Key (AK-1, AK-2): the same cell with every slot written in.

ownerRulings.ruling: A distinct option is also a findable preset skill (a new difficulty or a new skill); small tweaks stay plain options.
Part-whole bar: drawn on teaching pages, an option (default off) on practice pages.

No owner sign-off of skill or lesson cards for the lessons-first program: lanes decide the card lines from the standards and record them; the owner reviews finished work only. Scope: the CCSS BUILD lessons only. (The Signed line below records the lane's decision under this rule.)

misconceptions.error: counts the rows (or groups) as the total
reads one row or column too far on the chart
thinks turning the array changes the product
x 0 gives the other number (zero is 'nothing happens')
splits the wrong factor or drops a part in the distributive split
